name: to_sparse_bsr
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::to_sparse_bsr(Tensor self, int[2] blocksize, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. This definition models only that overload; it is representative, not exclusive. Original Gems pytest owns the full contract, including overload/keyword/return/error/mutation/alias behavior, and tests must never be narrowed, removed or have reference semantics adapted to fit this single signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::to_sparse_bsr(Tensor self, int[2] blocksize, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. Semantics (derived from the tests): converts a dense tensor into a block sparse BSR tensor by compressing the last two non-dense dimensions into a block matrix of blocksize (rows, cols); dense_dim (default None, meaning 0) selects how many trailing dimensions remain dense, and the two dimensions immediately before that dense tail form the block matrix, while the leading dimensions ahead of it stay separate batch dimensions in the sparse metadata. The result has layout torch.sparse_bsr with the same logical shape as the input, sparse_dim()==2, dense_dim()==effective dense_dim, crow_indices of shape lead + (n_row_blocks + 1,) (the leading batch dimensions are preserved separately, not merged into one compressed axis), and a values() tensor whose last 2 + dense_dim dimensions are blocksize + dense tail. The conversion is out of place for a dense self: for the non-contiguous view fixtures (transpose/offset/step/expand) the test checks that neither the logical input nor the real parent allocation behind the view is written, while the channels_last fixture materializes its own copy through to(memory_format=...) and therefore has no parent allocation to compare against. Blocksize is required (list/tuple; the test comment records, as measured, that the native operator also accepts a bool or int); dense_dim is keyword-capable with default None, and an omitted dense_dim must exercise the schema default. Errors remain pytest-owned: missing blocksize, wrong arity, zero/negative/fractional extents, blocksizes not dividing the matrix, negative or out-of-range dense_dim leaving no matrix, rank-0/rank-1 inputs, and a zero batch product. Overload-dependent behavior that this single-signature model does not express conditionally: test_to_sparse_bsr_sparse_source passes sparse COO/CSR/CSC/BSR/BSC inputs, and for an already-sparse-BSR source the test additionally asserts that the Gems result itself is the input object (res_out = flag_gems.to_sparse_bsr(inp, (2, 2)) with assert res_out is inp); because that identity assert is written against the Gems result, aliasing and any sparse-source-dependent behavior remain pytest concerns, not fields of this representative definition. Non-JSON ATen defaults: dense_dim's default was supplied as JSON null, which is the faithful rendering of the schema's None default; no non-JSON default needs string preservation here. The blocksize type_hint List[int] is a copy of the evidenced int[2] type; type_hint values are documentation only and generate no data. float8, bool, float64, special values, gradients/backward and a missing FlagGems kernel are all handled by the unchanged pytest/benchmark assets, not by this definition.
